title: ECMWF introduces AIFS-COMPO, a new AI system for atmospheric composition forecasting
key_facts: ECMWF introduced AIFS-COMPO, a data-driven AI system forecasting global atmospheric composition (aerosols and reactive gases) up to 10 days ahead.
The operational CAMS global forecast, run by ECMWF for the European Commission, covers five days, updated twice a day.
Initial evaluation shows competitive forecasts at substantially lower computational cost, with comparable or improved skill for several key species.
AIFS-COMPO is a forecasting model only: it starts from the operational CAMS analyses and relies on their satellite data assimilation.
It is experimental: it lacks time-varying emissions as inputs and forecasts fewer variables and chemical species, at lower resolution.
Laurence Rouil, Director of CAMS at ECMWF, says the operational CAMS system remains the benchmark for accuracy and reliability.
First charts are on the ECMWF website; the underlying data will be released later; a preprint is on arXiv.
quote_evidence: AIFS-COMPO currently produces forecasts out to 10 days, extending beyond the five-day horizon of the operational CAMS global atmospheric composition forecasts.
Initial evaluation of AIFS-COMPO shows that the data-driven approach can provide competitive forecasts at substantially lower computational cost.
AIFS-COMPO is currently an experimental system, with several areas of development under way.
why_it_matters_hint: Faster, cheaper air-quality forecasts that reach further ahead could support public health warnings.
notes: Performance claims are ECMWF's own initial evaluation; no outside review reported.
